headline: Energy Leads a Bruised Monday as Semiconductors and Homebuilders Bear the Brunt
body_html:
Monday's session closed with more losers than winners — 320 decliners against 228 advancers in a universe of 549 names — as geopolitical tension in the Middle East and inflation anxiety set the tone from the opening bell. Oil prices surged on Strait of Hormuz concerns, handing Energy a commanding 3.95% gain and making it the session's only sector to post a meaningful advance. Healthcare managed a modest 1.13% rise, and Software eked out a fractional 0.21% gain, but those bright spots were outnumbered.

The rotation away from rate-sensitive and cyclical names was pronounced. Homebuilders fell 2.48% and Semiconductors skidded 3.12%, with MaxLinear dropping 8.72% among the chip group's notable casualties. Industrials shed 1.29%, Consumer lost 0.78%, and Materials slipped 0.70%, completing a broadly defensive tilt that benefited hard assets over growth.

The standout mover of the day was N-able, which cratered 35.67% — a decline so severe it dwarfed every other name in the universe and will demand explanation when guidance or news surfaces. On the upside, Datadog surged 11.48%, a reminder that selective growth names can still attract conviction even on risk-off days. Monday's tape suggests the market remains torn between macro caution and pockets of earnings-driven optimism.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Anxiety Sends Energy Names Sharply Higher
briefs.body: Rising tensions around the Strait of Hormuz propelled oil prices and lifted Energy to a 3.95% session gain — the only sector in positive territory by a wide margin. Offshore-services names Valaris and Tidewater rose 8.57% and 8.16%, respectively, as traders priced in potential supply-route disruption.

briefs.headline: N-able Suffers a Stunning Single-Session Collapse
briefs.body: The software-management firm N-able plunged 35.67%, the sharpest decline across the entire 549-name universe on Monday. The magnitude of the drop implies a significant negative catalyst — likely a guidance revision or contract loss — though full details were still circulating after the close.

briefs.headline: Datadog Bucks the Growth Selloff with an 11% Surge
briefs.body: Observability-software specialist Datadog gained 11.48%, standing out as a rare conviction buy on an otherwise defensive Monday. The move suggests investors are distinguishing between cloud-infrastructure plays with durable demand and broader growth names that remain under pressure from the rate environment.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Extends Its Rough Patch
briefs.body: Semiconductors dropped 3.12%, the worst sector performance of the session, as inflation data on the horizon and global trade uncertainty weighed on the group. MaxLinear led declines within the cohort, falling 8.72%, adding to what has become a persistent period of underperformance for chip-related equities.

briefs.headline: Gold Retreats Slightly Even as Safe-Haven Demand Persists
briefs.body: Bullion edged lower from a recent seven-week high as traders awaited fresh U.S. inflation readings for directional clarity. The modest pullback did not signal a loss of safe-haven appetite — broader market breadth remained negative and defensive posturing was evident throughout Monday's session.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Finds Footing Amid Broad Market Weakness
briefs.body: Healthcare advanced 1.13%, the second-best sector on Monday, as investors rotated toward defensive names. LifeStance Health climbed 9.78% and BioMarin Pharmaceutical gained 7.95%, demonstrating that select biotech and services names could attract buyers even as cyclical sectors faced sustained selling pressure.
